scenario: AITA For Banning My Sisters Ex Husband From Coming to Family Events and Causing Drama? | So this situation has been going on for some time now and I’m turning to an outside source for critique. For context I’m a thirty six year old women, my sister is thirty four. My sister has three kids with her ex husband and I have four with my husband. They got divorced early 2019 because he’s been cheating on her with multiple women and even impregnanted TWO who both had abortions. This entire saga traumatized my younger sister and the divorce was rough. I’m completely disgusted with my ex brother in law and so is my entire inner family. We’ve completely cut contact with him. My sister is the only one that communicates with him. My parents, other siblings, extended family do not interact with him. I always host family events at my house. Birthdays, Easter, Christmas parties etc. My husband inherited a beautiful home so we have been the go to party throwers for years now. Ever since the whole divorce I don’t want my ex brother in law in my home. He’s no longer invited to any events. My sister was upset and said that her kids would be upset to not have their dad at big events like this. She said she hates him for cheating but accepts that she has kids with him so they are stuck together for life. But I have the right to not want someone I hate in my home and at my events. I stood by firmly and my husband agreed with me. Her kids got upset that I didn’t want their dad at any events and my kids now hate their ex uncle (even though I haven’t ever spoken to them about the situation). It was my daughters birthday this January and I was throwing a very extravagant party. I rented out an amusement park for the day and my daughters entire grade came. Parents of course as they are fourth graders and my sisters son wanted his father there and of course I let him know my rule stands. My sister got upset and says that she can fight her own battles and that banning him makes me an asshole. My sister has always allowed this guy to walk all over her and always defends him. Am I wrong for not wanting him at events and parties I throw? I just don’t see it.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to ban my sister's ex-husband from coming to family events that I host. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, my sister and her ex-husband had a really rough divorce in 2019 because he cheated on her with multiple women, and even impregnated two others who had abortions. That sounds really traumatic for my sister and the kids. I can see why I and the rest of the family would be disgusted with him and want to cut ties. I host these family events at my house, like birthdays, Easter, Christmas parties, and we've been known for throwing great parties. Since the divorce, I've made it clear that I don't want him in my home, and I haven't invited him to any events. My husband supports this decision. But my sister is upset because she thinks the kids would be upset if their dad isn't at big events. She hates him for cheating but acknowledges that they have kids together, so they're stuck together for life. I get that she's trying to maintain some relationship for the kids' sake, but I don't want someone I hate in my home. When it was my daughter's birthday this January, I went all out, renting an amusement park for the day, and even the kids from my sister's side wanted their dad there. I stuck to my rule, and my sister got upset, calling me a asshole. She's always let this guy walk all over her and defend him, which is frustrating. So, am I wrong for not wanting him at my events? I don't see it that way. I have the right to decide who comes into my home and participates in my family events. But I'm also concerned about the impact on the kids and the relationship with my sister. Maybe I should consider why my sister is so insistent. Is it because she feels guilty or doesn't want to completely cut him out? Or does she think it's better for the kids to have both parents involved? On the other hand, I have to protect my own family's peace and security. Perhaps there's a middle ground. Maybe the ex-husband can attend events in a more neutral setting, not at my house, so I don't feel like I'm compromising my boundaries. Or maybe the kids can spend time with him separately, not during our family gatherings. I also need to communicate better with my sister. She feels like I'm making her fight her own battles, but I'm trying to protect my family. Maybe we can find a way to respect both our needs. In the end, I think it's important to prioritize the well-being of the kids and maintain harmony within the family. If banning him from my events is causing unnecessary drama and affecting the kids, maybe I need to reconsider my stance, even if it's difficult.
